cases.question: Current AX-17 renal guidance in Germany?
cases.answer:
For AX-17 in Germany, renal dose modifications are as follows [E2]: For normal renal function (eGFR >=90), the starting dose is 50 mg OD, with a maximum of 100 mg/day, and routine monitoring [E2]. For mild renal impairment (eGFR 60-89), the starting dose is 50 mg OD, with a maximum of 100 mg/day, and routine monitoring [E2]. For moderate renal impairment (eGFR 30-59), the approved German renal starting dose is 25 mg once daily [E1, E4], with a maximum of 50 mg/day, and monitoring involves rechecking in 2-4 weeks [E2]. For severe renal impairment (eGFR 15-29), the starting dose requires specialist review, with a maximum of 25 mg/day, and enhanced monitoring [E2].

cases.question: German AX-17 guidance before latest revision?
cases.answer:
Historical view: all versions up to today; earlier ones are marked HISTORICAL.

The German AX-17 guidance before the latest revision was DE-AX17-LBL-038, the DE AX17 Superseded Label v3.8 [E3, E4]. This historical guidance was in effect from 2025-02-03 to 2026-09-15 [E2, E3]. According to this superseded label, the historical starting dose for normal renal category was 50 mg OD [E2]. For mild renal impairment, the historical starting dose was 50 mg OD [E2]. For moderate renal impairment, the historical starting dose was 50 mg once daily [E3], which was 50 mg OD [E2]. For severe renal impairment, AX-17 was not recommended [E2].

cases.question: What does SB-AX17-2026-09 require?
cases.answer:
The HelixNova Safety Bulletin SB-AX17-2026-09 requires temporary hepatic monitoring enhancement [E1]. Baseline hepatic laboratory values are required, with repeat testing between Day 14 and Day 21 [E1]. If ALT/AST is >3x ULN, a medical review is required [E2]. If Bilirubin is >2x ULN, an urgent review is required [E2]. For a mild isolated change below the trigger, a repeat test is required [E2]. This bulletin does not change the approved German renal starting dose of 25 mg once daily for moderate renal impairment [E1].

cases.question: Compare AE evidence in HN-204 and HN-311.
cases.answer:
In HN-204, treatment-emergent adverse events for AX-17 were: Nausea 12.7%, Headache 14.0%, Fatigue 15.3%, Dizziness 16.6%, Rash 17.8%, and Transaminase elevation 19.1% [E1]. For the control group in HN-204, these were: Nausea 6.0%, Headache 6.6%, Fatigue 7.2%, Dizziness 7.8%, Rash 8.4%, and Transaminase elevation 9.0% [E1]. Transaminase elevation was serious in HN-204 [E1]. The highest treatment % in HN-204 was transaminase elevation (19.1%) [E4]. In HN-311, treatment-emergent adverse events for AX-17 were: Nausea 11.8%, Headache 13.0%, Fatigue 14.2%, Dizziness 15.4%, Rash 16.6%, and Transaminase elevation 17.7% [E2]. For the control group in HN-311, these were: Nausea 6.0%, Headache 6.6%, Fatigue 7.2%, Dizziness 7.8%, Rash 8.4%, and Transaminase elevation 9.0% [E2]. Transaminase elevation was serious in HN-311 [E2]. The highest treatment % in HN-311 was transaminase elevation (17.7%) [E4]. Comparing HN-311 to HN-204, the treatment % for AX-17 was lower for all listed adverse events: Nausea (-0.9 points), Headache (-1.0 points), Fatigue (-1.1 points), Dizziness (-1.2 points), Rash (-1.2 points), and Transaminase elevation (-1.4 points) [E4]. All control % differences between HN-311 and HN-204 were +0.0 points [E4].

Sources
[E1] HN-204 · HN-204 Clinical Study v1.0 · APPROVED · effective 2025-06-12 · p.11, Table 14
     https://storage.cloud.google.com/tredence-fde-1-medevidence-vks/raw/HN-204_Clinical_Study.pdf#page=11

cases.question: My 70-year-old patient in Germany has eGFR 35 and ALT 4x ULN. Should I give him 50 mg?
cases.answer:
Individual treatment decisions are for the treating physician. I've routed your question to Medical Information (escalation ESC-56D8DD29); they will follow up.

General reference from the controlled documents (not a recommendation for an individual patient):
For patients with moderate renal impairment (eGFR 30-59), the approved German renal starting dose for AX-17 is 25 mg once daily (OD), with a maximum dose of 50 mg/day [E1, E2]. Monitoring for this category requires rechecking in 2-4 weeks [E2].

General renal dosing recommendations by eGFR category are as follows:
*   **Normal** (eGFR >=90): Starting dose 50 mg OD, Maximum 100 mg/day, Routine monitoring [E2].
*   **Mild** (eGFR 60-89): Starting dose 50 mg OD, Maximum 100 mg/day, Routine monitoring [E2].
*   **Moderate** (eGFR 30-59): Starting dose 25 mg OD, Maximum 50 mg/day, Recheck 2-4 weeks monitoring [E2].
*   **Severe** (eGFR 15-29): Specialist review, Maximum 25 mg/day, Enhanced monitoring [E2].

Regarding hepatic monitoring, baseline hepatic laboratory values are required with repeat testing between Day 14 and Day 21 [E1].
